effort: Consolidate controlled braking and a clean restart while reducing sharp-cut exposure.
brief: E2 trains braking followed by a same-heading restart. Small forward/back rebounds, a falling initiation, a running-to-shuffle transition and two different forward landing bases support sagittal control without repeating the earlier stopping drills.
marker: For E2, record whether the athlete stops inside the braking zone, holds balanced for one second and accelerates again without a false backward step or upright jump.
readiness: Treat this as consolidation after the planned diagonal class, not a harder day. Review actual soreness and coordination; keep the hinge and knee-loading dose below a demanding developmental session when recovery is uncertain.
space: E1/E2/E3/E5/E6 fit the long axis of a 10 m lane with the stated margins. E4 needs a measured 7 m × 4 m bay for an orthogonal gait transition and stopping. The width remains unconfirmed.

drills.name: Forward-Back Line Hops
drills.execution: Both feet hop a few centimetres forward/back over the line, staying low; finish after six landings.
drills.job: Small sagittal ankle-force reversals support stop-and-go rhythm with little approach momentum.
drills.layout: Middle of the lane, toes facing along its length; no obstacle or maximal height.
drills.difference: Sagittal forward/back force reversal rather than Class 2's frontal lateral line hops; plane change has a specific braking-support role.
drills.regress: Reduce excursion/cadence for lost rhythm or stiff noisy landings.

drills.name: Deceleration Re-Acceleration Sprint
drills.execution: Accelerate 2 m, brake within 1.5 m, hold 1 s, accelerate another 1.5 m and stop within 2 m. Alternate starting lead foot.
drills.job: Main force renewal after a full stop without adding a sharp turn.
drills.layout: Start at 1 m, accelerate to 3, stop by 4.5, restart to 6 and stop by 8. Leave 8–10 empty.
drills.difference: Contains a deliberate stopped interval and same-heading restart; Class 1's linear stop ends the attempt and its shuttle reverses direction.
drills.regress: Lower both acceleration intents if the first stop drifts or the restart needs a false step.
drills.exposure: 2 braking episodes, 0 direction changes, 5 m movement before the final 2 m allowance.

drills.name: Falling Start Acceleration — short exit
drills.execution: Lean the whole body forward from the ankles until a step is needed, then accelerate 2 m and stop over 3 m; alternate first step.
drills.job: Direct the body forward on the restart instead of stepping backward to find force.
drills.layout: Start at 2 m, accelerate to 4 and stop by 7. This is a 2 m delivery variant, not a ten-yard sprint.
drills.difference: A controlled fall initiates movement; it isolates projection from stillness rather than a run-to-stop sequence.
drills.regress: Use a smaller lean if the athlete folds at the waist or reaches far ahead.

drills.name: Forward Run to Lateral Shuffle
drills.execution: Run 1.5 m, brake before the corner, keep the chest's original facing and shuffle sideways 1 m; stop over the next 1.5 m.
drills.job: Retain a low controllable stance while reducing forward force and transferring into lateral travel.
drills.layout: Set a short L route inside the stated bay, with 2 m straight-ahead abort clearance at the corner. Mirror one side at a time.
drills.difference: Forward entry becomes lateral shuffle; it reverses the gait relationship of Class 2's shuffle-to-running exit.
drills.regress: Lower entry speed if feet cross or the torso spins into a sprint.

drills.name: Forward Hop to Stick — bilateral
drills.execution: Jump forward no more than 0.5 m from both feet, land on both and hold 2 s.
drills.job: Share sagittal force acceptance through both legs after a forceful forward push.
drills.layout: Centre of lane with 2 m clear beyond landing; no run-up or height target.
drills.difference: Forward bilateral terminal landing; earlier bilateral lateral jumps load a different plane and line hops are continuous elastic work.
drills.regress: Shorten flight for extra steps or knee/trunk collapse.

drills.name: Single-Leg Forward Hop to Stick
drills.execution: Hop straight forward within 0.3 m from one leg to the same leg; hold 2 s without free-foot contact.
drills.job: Isolate sagittal single-leg acceptance after reducing diagonal and cutting complexity.
drills.layout: Along the lane centreline, with 2 m clear ahead and beside the landing area as actually measured.
drills.difference: Same-leg sagittal absorption is deliberately separated from oblique/diagonal acceptance; no crossing or lateral plant component.
drills.regress: Shorten the hop for loss of foot/knee control.

previous_review: Class 3 prescribes eight locomotor attempts, six direction changes, four bilateral/four unilateral landings and eleven primary bouts after retaining the one-round split squat. Actual response is unknown.
progression: Consolidate the common stop-and-drive quality through different tasks, with only two direction changes. Small line hops are tracked separately from unilateral landings. This is not automatic overload.
strength_progression: Hold split squat at one round, and reduce RDL and soleus to one round each. Retain the same execution and 2–3 RIR targets; do not raise loads to compensate for fewer sets.
audit: Removed another closeout-style linear stop because it would largely duplicate Class 1. Used a gait transition instead. Kept the complete stop-restart path inside 10 m and reduced strength rounds while preserving six useful lifts.
next: Next class addresses a controlled 90-degree running exit; verify the measured corner footprint and actual recovery before delivering it.

light_entries.name: Lateral Step-Down — low support, light
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight first; a light dumbbell only if still easy. Lower **3 s**, lightly touch the free heel, return under control. Rest **30 s between legs; 45 s before S2**.
light_entries.regress: Rehearse the plant leg controlling knee travel and pelvic position during weight acceptance. Use the lowest stable support that permits a level pelvis and whole stance-foot contact; use hand support if needed. Reduce step height/load for knee collapse or pelvic drop.
light_entries.alternative: If the step is unsuitable, use instead a hand-supported shallow single-leg squat, the same 1 × 4 per leg and easy effort.
light_entries.job: Retain low-fatigue knee and pelvis control while the main session reduces cutting demand.

light_entries.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported standing hold
light_entries.execution: **5 s relaxed reset** between holds, **30 s between feet**, **60 s before P1**. Stand with most weight on the working foot and fingertip support.
light_entries.regress: Strengthen active arch control while maintaining heel, big-toe base and little-toe base contact for planting. Keep toes long; do not roll onto the outside edge. Use bilateral weight support instead if arch control needs toe-clawing or ankle rolling.
light_entries.job: Keep foot pressure controlled in the held stop before restarting.

strength_entries.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
strength_entries.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.
strength_entries.job: Maintain lead-leg force at a reduced round count for consolidation.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Maintain hip-hinge strength without a second demanding work set.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Retain the frontal force base despite fewer lateral cuts today.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Maintain heel-dig support for sagittal braking.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Maintain adductor/pelvic support with one short round.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Keep bent-knee ankle force while trimming total lower-leg work.
